audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Wukong/Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser against a packet levelChart of Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Wukong. audit.why: 50.57% over 471 games: an even lane Mordekaiser bends with his 2-3 and 6 spikes, and Wukong reclaims in teamfights on items. The chart gave Mordekaiser the 2+ item row that its own caption gives to Wukong.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Skill / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Wukong as one atomic paired group, with ratings and the two contradicting phases[N].why lines rewritten.

audit.why: Four spikes[] present and correctly timed — Mordekaiser's level 2-3 Q+W window, Realm of Death at 6, the first-item magic spike, and Wukong's late teamfight window. Only the naming inside them was wrong, not the timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flags it directly: the content layer never names a single Wukong ability. Every reference is a generic paraphrase — 'his Q armor-shred', 'his W decoy', 'W clone', 'E-dash', 'R spin', 'his R knockup' — across whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[3] and the prose. A player reading this page cannot map any of it to a cooldown bar. Separately, missingInteractions flags that Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto-attack reset and nothing on the page carries that tell.
audit.why: Real ability names are the difference between advice a player can act on and advice they have to translate. The full layer already uses the names — the content layer, which is what renders in the level chart and spike cards, does not.
audit.corrected: Replaced the paraphrases with Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone throughout whys[1..3], whys[6] and spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[3] — all four names confirmed against packet.enemyAbilities. Added the Crushing Blow auto-reset tell to dontsFull[2].d, whose heading already read 'Trade into his Q shred' but whose body was the generic tradeBad string.
